translations: When the Eight Immortals reached the edge of the East Sea, the wind was pushing waves onto the shore in neat, rolling rows. Tieguai Li was the first to stop. He planted his iron crutch firmly into the sand and declared, “The road ends here.”
Zhang Guolao, who was facing backward, peered over his shoulder. “There’s a road. It’s just that it’s made entirely of water.”
“That’s what we call *no* road.”
“If you stand upright, sure, there’s nothing to walk on. But if you look at it upside down, the whole world is open for travel.”
Lü Dongbin couldn’t take it anymore. “First, figure out which way is up for yourself, then try giving directions to the rest of the world.”

An old fisherman, who had been pulling in his nets, heard the argument and waded over to ask where they were headed. Han Zhongli pointed to the other side of the sea and said they needed to cross the East Sea. The fisherman looked at the eight strangers, then at his tiny boat. His face showed the exact expression of a man whose livelihood had just landed a huge contract, but who was terrified his boat might sink under the weight of it.
“The boat can hold you,” he said. “It will just be a bit crowded.”
Lan Caihe hugged his flower basket to his chest. “I don’t take up much space. My flowers do.”
Han Xiangzi added, “My flute doesn’t take up space either.”
Cao Guojiu adjusted his official robes and hat. “People can squeeze, but etiquette cannot be squeezed.”
He Xiangu laughed. “If we divide it up like that, only the etiquette will be on the boat, and the rest of us will be standing on the shore waving goodbye.”

The old fisherman wasn’t sure if these people were making a plan or tearing each other down, so he tried again. “The waves are big today in the East Sea. If you really want to cross, it’s safer to take the boat.”

Tieguai Li shook his head. They weren’t refusing the boat because they looked down on mortal vessels; they simply didn’t want to cram eight of themselves onto the small boat the fisherman relied on for his living, forcing him to risk his life for the ride. Han Zhongli unfurled his palm-leaf fan to block the sea breeze, Zhang Guolao tapped his drum, Lü Dongbin rested his hand on his sword hilt, He Xiangu held her lotus, Lan Caihe lifted his flower basket, Han Xiangzi took out his jade flute, and Cao Guojiu unfastened his jade tablet. Each of them had their own special skills. If they still crushed the fisherman’s boat until it groaned in protest, even the wooden planks would laugh at them when the story got out.
Lü Dongbin spoke up. “No boat. We’ll each cross using our own talents. We won’t use a mortal’s livelihood to show off our divine power.”
Zhang Guolao asked, “Can I borrow a bit of my companions’ power?”
“Don’t borrow yet. Wait until your own power isn’t enough.”
“Then I’ll keep that in mind, so you can’t deny it later.”

Everyone agreed. The old fisherman retreated to higher ground, still worried, and warned them to turn back if the waves looked dangerous. The Eight Immortals didn’t treat his concern as a joke. They thanked him sincerely, then stepped together to the water’s edge.

The seawash rose up, covering the footprints they had just left. None of the eight stepped back, but no one rushed to throw their magical treasures into the water either. If showing off their skills was just a race to be first, the other seven would have nothing to do but watch. Instead, they decided on an order, so each person could clearly show their own path.

Aman crouched by the reef, clutching his green bamboo slips. He wrote from Tieguai Li to Cao Guojiu, then counted the names again to be sure. Lan Caihe leaned in and asked, “Is that enough for eight?”
Aman said, “It is. But if you keep walking back and forth, I might accidentally write *Sixteen Immortals Crossing the Sea*.”
He Xiangu pulled Lan Caihe back to his spot. “Stand still. Don’t add extra people to the historical record.”

Aman spread the green bamboo slips on the damp rock. He dipped his brush tip into the salty mist of the sea breeze and wrote the three characters “No Boat.” He then rolled up the slips and stepped back carefully, afraid a wave might sweep them away. Standing on the fine sand at the shore, his toe hit a smooth shell. He nearly slipped but steadied himself, careful not to startle the eight immortals before him.

On the sea, the waves of the East Sea rose one after another, like curious children playing. The rolling white foam shimmered with silver light in the sunset. Each wave seemed to be sizing up these eight immortals who refused to take a mortal boat, eager to see what magical treasures they would use to get across.

He Xiangu gently steadied Lan Caihe and whispered, “Stand still, don’t add extra people to the historical record.” Lan Caihe nodded, gripping a slightly worn golden staff in his hand. He muttered, “If this staff of mine falls into the sea, I’m afraid it’ll turn into a conch shell.” With that, he flicked the staff lightly. The tip traced a silver arc in the air and tapped the crest of a wave, sparking a tiny flame, as if lighting a small candle on the ocean.
Seeing this, Aman quickly raised his bamboo slips to keep them from blowing away in the wind. He frowned slightly and murmured, “That spark is quite bright. It looks like a lamp in the sea.”

Right after that, Zhang Guolao leaned on his crutch and slowly walked to the water’s edge. He looked up at the waves and smiled. “This isn’t just an ordinary crutch. It can turn into a bridge wherever I go.” With that, he tapped the crutch lightly. Instantly, it transformed into a pale blue arched bridge spanning between two wave crests. Unfortunately, the bridge was too light. As soon as a small splash hit it, the crutch-bridge creaked and collapsed. Zhang Guolao had to grab his crutch to steady himself, shaking his head with a laugh. “Looks like I need to practice my bridge-stabilizing skills.”
